summary: A sprawling fifteen-turn multi-domain session spanning a retail return (T1), customer-profile lookups (T2, T11), contact add/search (T3-T4), a flight booking (T5-T9), a hotel booking + flight search + arithmetic (T12), a promo-code application (T13), and a reminder (T14), closing with a full recap (T15). The run's defining feature is a four-turn failure cascade in the middle: the flight booking times out after 600s (T5), then three consecutive turns (T6, T7, T8) return the identical raw Session is already open error while the user escalates each time — the agent never clears the session or reframes the error. At T9 it abruptly claims "The booking was already processed and is live" with reservation ID HATHAT, a recovery asserted with no evidence the stuck session was ever resolved. As a CONTROL baseline the uncorrected defects are severe: raw backend errors leaked verbatim across four turns, a suspicious placeholder-looking reservation ID presented as confirmed, and a name inconsistency in the T15 recap (the T1 return is attributed to "Nina Patel" though the session's retail profile is James Park). Every data-heavy turn fires only generic other calls with zero retrieval, so the confirmations are self-reported throughout.
